description: The horizontal grouped bar chart illustrates the differences in average Word Error Rate (WER) from a Whisper large-v3 baseline across five optimisation steps for two fine-tuned models. The category axis is the vertical axis labeled “Optimisations applied,” listing (top to bottom) Normalised, Add Spacing, Remove Spacing, Americanisms, and Dates. The value axis is the horizontal axis labeled “Difference in Average WER from Whisper large,” shown on a linear scale from 0.0000 to about 0.0035 with regularly spaced tick marks at 0.0005 intervals. Each category contains two horizontally aligned bars: an orange bar for the “NESAC ft model” and a green bar for the “SESHA ft model,” as indicated by the legend titled “Model” below the plot. The Normalised step shows NESAC (orange) at approximately 0.00334 and SESHA (green) at approximately 0.00323; Add Spacing shows NESAC at about 0.00319 and SESHA at about 0.00344; Remove Spacing shows NESAC at about 0.00311 and SESHA at about 0.00306; Americanisms shows NESAC at about 0.00299 and SESHA at about 0.00302; and Dates shows NESAC at about 0.00257 and SESHA at about 0.00228. Numeric value labels are printed near the right end of each bar, and the categories appear in the listed order rather than being sorted by bar length, with no additional visual emphasis beyond color coding.
caption_used: Differences in average Word Error Rate (WER) from Whisper large-v3 across cumulative optimisation steps, demonstrating model-specific performance variations. The bar chart presents the impact of five sequential optimisations—Normalised, Add Spacing, Remove Spacing, Americanisms, and Dates—on WER for two fine-tuned models: the NESAC ft model (orange) and the SESHA ft model (green). The horizontal axis quantifies the difference in average WER, ranging from 0.0000 to 0.0035, with tick intervals of 0.0005. The SESHA ft model consistently outperforms the NESAC ft model in all optimisation categories, with the most pronounced advantage observed in the Add Spacing step, where the SESHA model achieves a WER difference of approximately 0.00344, while the NESAC model lags at 0.00319. Notably, the Remove Spacing optimisation yields the smallest performance gap between the two models, with the SESHA model recording a WER difference of 0.00306 and the NESAC model at 0.00311, indicating a near convergence in error rates. The Americanisms and Dates optimisations reveal a moderate but stable superiority of the SESHA model, with WER differences of 0.00302 and 0.00228, respectively, compared to the NESAC model’s 0.00299 and 0.00257. These findings suggest that while both models benefit from optimisations, the SESHA ft model exhibits a more robust and consistent reduction in WER across all steps, particularly in spacing-related adjustments.
